reading.title: The Psychology of Flow
reading.intro_zh: 这篇拓展阅读不复述孤舟钓鱼，而是借心理学家 Csikszentmihalyi 的“flow（心流）”概念，解释为什么有人会为活动本身、而非结果去投入；内容改编自一篇发表于 Frontiers in Psychology 的同行评议论文。

source.title: Investigating the "Flow" Experience: Key Conceptual and Operational Issues

passage: When the narrator in Lesson 20 keeps fishing without catching anything, his friends measure the morning by an empty bag and conclude that it is a waste of time. Psychologists, however, would describe his quiet contentment in very different terms. The Hungarian-American researcher Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi spent decades studying what he called "flow", an optimal state of consciousness in which a person becomes so absorbed in an activity that nothing outside it seems to matter. The defining feature of such moments is not the prize at the end but the experience itself, which people report as so enjoyable that they will pursue it for its own sake, even at considerable cost.

Activities of this kind are described as autotelic, a word formed from the Greek roots for "self" and "goal": the doing is its own reward. Flow tends to appear when the difficulty of a task is delicately matched to a person's skill, neither so trivial that it breeds boredom nor so demanding that it provokes anxiety. Under those conditions, attention narrows to an intense focus, action and awareness merge, self-consciousness fades, and the passage of time becomes distorted. Crucially, researchers distinguish between the conditions that make flow possible and the subjective experience itself, warning that an external scoreboard captures almost none of what makes the activity worthwhile. By this account, the solitary fisherman is not failing at all; he has simply chosen a goal his friends cannot see, and is succeeding at it in silence.

questions.question: What is the main point the passage makes about the fisherman's morning?
options: His friends are right that an empty bag proves the time was wasted.
He should learn better fishing techniques to catch more fish.
Psychology suggests the value lies in the absorbing experience, not the catch.
Flow can only be reached by professional athletes and artists.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文用心理学的“flow”概念重新解释那位钓鱼人：价值在于沉浸的过程本身，而不是钓到的鱼，因此 C 正确。

questions.question: According to the passage, when does flow tend to appear?
options: When a task's difficulty is carefully matched to a person's skill.
When the activity is as easy as possible so it never feels stressful.
When there is a clear prize or external reward at the end.
When several people compete against one another for a score.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说 flow 出现在任务难度与个人技能“delicately matched”时，既不会太简单也不会太难，故选 A。

questions.question: What does the passage say happens once a person enters flow?
options: They become more aware of the people watching them.
They feel time passing more slowly and clearly than usual.
They lose all interest in the activity within minutes.
Attention narrows, action and awareness merge, and self-consciousness fades.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段列出进入 flow 后的表现：注意力高度集中、行动与意识融合、自我意识消退，时间感被扭曲，故选 D。

questions.question: What can we infer about why the friends misjudge the fisherman?
options: They secretly envy how many fish he catches.
They judge by a visible scoreboard that misses the experience he values.
They have never seen anyone fish from a boat before.
They believe fishing is physically dangerous for him.
questions.explanation_zh: 文章指出“an external scoreboard captures almost none of what makes the activity worthwhile”，朋友用看得见的结果衡量，自然看不到他真正在意的体验，故选 B。

questions.question: In this passage, the word "autotelic" describes an activity that is:
options: done mainly to win money or public recognition.
valuable only when it produces a measurable result.
performed for its own sake, with the doing as its own reward.
too difficult for an ordinary person to complete.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中解释 autotelic 由希腊词根“self”和“goal”构成，意为“the doing is its own reward”，即为活动本身而做，故选 C。

writing.intro_zh: 今天抓五个 Lesson 20 的核心句式，但把语境升级到更抽象、更成熟的层面：做了很久却没有预期回报、实际结果与期待相反、长期付出之后、被别人判定为浪费时间，以及说清楚自己真正投入的过程。

patterns.title: without ...ing anything
patterns.source: I often fish for hours without catching anything.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 without + 动词-ing + anything 写“投入了很久，却没有得到预期回报”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你长期坚持某个爱好或计划，外人看不到任何可衡量的成果，你却从过程中获得了别的东西。
patterns.sample: For three years I have practised the piano almost every evening without entering anything or earning a single award.
patterns.tip_zh: without 后面接动词-ing，比如 entering, finding, winning, earning；anything 放在句尾能强调“什么可衡量的结果也没有”。

patterns.title: Instead of ...ing
patterns.source: Instead of catching fish, they catch old boots and rubbish.
patterns.focus_zh: Instead of + 动词-ing 用来写“本来以为会得到 A，结果却是更有价值的 B”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你本可以追求分数、名次或奖项，你却选择了某个更抽象、更持久的收获。
patterns.sample: Instead of chasing the highest score in every exam, I have learned to value the slow, patient pleasure of understanding an idea.
patterns.tip_zh: Instead of 后面用动词-ing；逗号后面写真正发生的结果或真正有价值的部分。

patterns.title: After having spent ...
patterns.source: After having spent whole mornings on the river, I always go home with an empty bag.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式先写“已经投入了很长时间”，再写最后那个不完美但真实的结果，故事感很强。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你投入了整个学期、整个夏天或很多年去做某件事之后，最后带着一个不闪亮但真实的结果。
patterns.sample: After having spent an entire summer rebuilding the same model engine, I returned to school with nothing to show but a calmer mind.
patterns.tip_zh: After having spent 后面接时间或经历；逗号后面接结果，不一定是成功结果。

patterns.title: It's a waste of time
patterns.source: You must give up fishing! It's a waste of time.
patterns.focus_zh: a waste of time 是别人的判断：他们只看结果，所以觉得这件事不值得。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写别人用看得见的“计分板”评判某个需要耐心或慢慢享受的过程是浪费时间。
patterns.sample: My relatives still insist that hours spent reading novels are a waste of time unless they raise my grades.
patterns.tip_zh: 注意这个句式常常是在表达某人的看法，不一定代表事实；可以写 My relatives said... 或 They thought...。

patterns.title: only interested in ...ing
patterns.source: I am only interested in sitting in a boat and doing nothing at all!
patterns.focus_zh: 用 only interested in + 动词-ing 说清楚真正投入的是过程，而不是外人期待的结果。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你并不只是想赢、完成或得到表扬，你真正投入的是某个能让你完全沉浸其中的过程。
patterns.sample: I am only interested in losing myself in the quiet rhythm of sketching, long after everyone else has gone home.
patterns.tip_zh: interested in 后面接动词-ing；可以用 losing myself in... 这样更成熟的表达来写“完全沉浸”。
